Hi Aisha — thanks for the note. Attached is our exported availability slice for 2027-06-05 through 2027-06-06 (uptime-report-20270605-20270610.csv) plus an initial credit worksheet (credit-calc-worksheet.xlsx). Summary:

- Redwood observed three degraded intervals tied to a routing configuration rollback: 2027-06-05T23:48:00Z — 2027-06-05T23:55:00Z (7 min), 2027-06-06T00:22:00Z — 2027-06-06T00:39:00Z (17 min), and 2027-06-06T01:03:00Z — 2027-06-06T02:15:00Z (72 min). Total impacted minutes: 96.
- Per contract, we calculate service credit as (downtime minutes / billed minutes in period) * monthly recurring fee prorated to the affected service. I've included line-by-line math in the spreadsheet so you can trace numbers back to raw timestamps.

We want to make sure any credit issued is aligned with your AR process. If your team prefers Redwood to issue a draft credit memo for internal review, we can do that once we align on final uptime windows.

Cc'ing Marissa (billing) and Sean (support lead) to pick up approvals if this moves forward.

Quick internal —

I reviewed Rachel's worksheet. Two items we should confirm before issuing any memo:
1) Billing period denominator: Helios is on monthly billing; confirm whether they want the credit applied to the invoice for June (recommended) or as an immediate one-off refund. If they take invoice credit we need HubSpot note and approval from finance.
2) Overlap with customer-side mitigation: Helios triggered a failover at 00:30 UTC — we should ensure we are not double-counting minutes where their failover partially restored service. Rachel, can you add a column tagging minutes as "Redwood-only", "Helios-failover", or "shared" based on our telemetry?

If the 96 minutes hold after tagging, the preliminary credit estimate on the worksheet is $23,400 (applies to their Dedicated tier). I can prepare a memo template for signature once Sean confirms the final window.

-Marissa
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Downtime credit breakdown & attribution — Helios Labs

Thanks — looked through the CSV. Rachel, good call on the three intervals. I cross-checked our per-region KV cache logs and can confirm the first two intervals were Redwood-initiated regressions; the long window (01:03–02:15 UTC) partially overlaps with Helios's failover activity (00:30–01:10 UTC).

I updated the worksheet with a "source_attribution" column and marked 40 of the 72 minutes in the final window as "shared" (their failover accounted for restoration on some nodes). After re-run, the adjusted impacted minutes = 64. Revised preliminary credit = $15,600.

Grace, Karthik — tagging you to confirm there's no contractual clause that requires a different denominator for shared events. If not, Marissa please proceed with draft memo.

-Sean
Support Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
